correctness.rationale: Every non-simple accepting walk in a forest contains a two-step directed reversal; duplication gives every larger accepted length of the same parity. Conversely an eventual parity tail is realized by a directed path with a terminal 2-cycle. A regular language has a finite eventual period and is represented by a path into an even simple cycle. For the one-hole family, an accepting walk of length \(m+2\) must be simple, because removing any immediate reversal would wrongly accept \(m\); the path construction attains the resulting \(m+3\)-state lower bound. All boundary conditions and orientations were considered.

value.rationale: The newly established general bipartite-cactus representation makes the exact threshold for lowering undirected support treewidth from two to one a natural structural question. The complete unary-language classification answers it, while the one-hole cofinite family measures an exact and unbounded state cost within the forest class.
